RQ3.rationale: The workflow explicitly integrates pre-physical Phase-0/Pre-Phase A verification by transforming the MAM into a ForPlan simulation and checking operation requirements using battery charge and memory/data results before driving flight-software implementation.

RQ1: CubeSat missions are modeled through a Cyber-Physical operation-scenario abstraction implemented as a Capella SysML-based Class Diagram MAM.
A reusable abstract MAM covers equipment, orbit, solar panels, battery pack, mass memory, ground stations, ROIs, and predefined equipment operation functions.

Limited behavioral knowledge is handled by parameterized high-level operations such as AlwaysOn, OnGroundStation, TimedOp, and RoiOP, hiding ForPlan source-code and Julia scripting details from users.
RQ2: Claimed value centers on requirements verification, visual configuration, simulator usability, faster scenario iteration, integration of model artifacts with simulation, and stakeholder decision support.
Reliability is only indirectly motivated through avoiding issues/failures from skipped systems engineering; no reliability metric, fault analysis, or operational evidence is provided.
Reproducibility and integrability are partially supported by the Capella-to-Julia-to-ForPlan transformation, but no open assets or independent reuse evidence are reported.
RQ3: Verification is integrated before physical implementation by generating ForPlan inputs from the MAM and simulating power/data operation scenarios in Phase-0/Pre-Phase A.
NCBR2 verification evidence includes battery charge and memory usage simulations used to infer stable power and data balances.
The final feasible scenario was reported as an input to on-board flight software development, but no physical EPS integration test is reported.

Capella Class Diagram supports only one metalevel, so the authors had to define well-formed constraints to make the models interpretable.

The EPS representation is limited to power-budget-relevant battery, solar, and equipment power parameters, not detailed EPS electrical architecture, control, fault behavior, or reliability modeling.
Requirements are checked through simulation outputs but are not modeled as formal requirement artifacts with explicit traceability links.
